summary.headline: Meghmani Organics FY26 standalone revenue rose 4% to INR 2,091 crore and EBITDA 27% to INR 228.7 crore, but Q4 standalone EBITDA was only INR 26.2 crore.
summary.overview: FY26 was a difficult year: US tariffs, a weaker export environment and the US-Iran war pushed raw material costs up while realisations stayed broadly flat. Standalone EBITDA recovered 27% for the full year, but Q4 remained thin, with Crop Protection margin near 9% and Pigments near 3%. Management suspended TiO2 operations as unviable after the anti-dumping duty was withdrawn and sulphuric acid prices spiked. Management guided to Crop Protection margins of 15-17% in FY27, double-digit Crop Protection top-line growth, and a Nano fertiliser ramp-up, and announced an amalgamation of two subsidiaries and a Brazil subsidiary.

financial_highlights.change: EBITDA up 24% YoY; margin vs 6.9% prior year

segments.name: Crop Protection (FY26)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,631 crore (about 78% of standalone revenue), EBITDA INR 244 crore, margin 15%; production about 40,371 MT at about 72% utilisation. Q4 revenue INR 348.6 crore, EBITDA INR 31.3 crore, margin about 9%.

segments.name: Pigments (FY26)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 461 crore (about 22% of revenue), EBITDA INR 15 crore, margin 3.3%; production about 13,191 MT at 40% utilisation. Q4 revenue INR 108 crore, EBITDA INR 3.2 crore, margin about 3%.

segments.name: Crop Nutrition
segments.commentary: Nano fertiliser products (Nano DAP, Nano NPK, Nano Zinc) received Ministry of Agriculture approval, to be made at Sanand, Gujarat with no additional capex. Commercial production expected in the Kharif season; Nano Urea is the key product, with about 7-8 products in the basket. No segment financials disclosed.

segments.name: Titanium Dioxide (Kilburn)
segments.commentary: Operations temporarily suspended as commercially unviable after the anti-dumping duty withdrawal, higher sulphuric acid and utility costs. Anti-dumping matter is under DGTR review.

guidance_outlook: Crop Protection: management expects EBITDA margin within 15-17% in FY27, and double-digit top-line growth with better profitability than Q4.
Pigments: top line of about INR 500-600 crore; FY27 profitability expected to be better than FY26's 3.3% margin, though not dramatically so.
Crop Nutrition: significant growth in top line and bottom line over the next 2-5 years; management declined to give quarter-wise timing and said FY27 as a whole will show growth.
Capex: no significant capex in FY27; routine capex of INR 35-40 crore. Working capital to improve through inventory and receivable-day reduction.
Dividend: management said it will try to provide a reasonably good dividend in FY27, subject to Board approval.
Renewable energy: 3.3 MW wind-solar hybrid power agreement, taking renewable share of energy use above 50%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company pay a dividend, given no dividend in recent years?
qa_highlights.answer: No dividend was declared for FY26; management said it will try to provide a reasonably good dividend in FY27, subject to Board approval, based on better revenue and profitability.

qa_highlights.question: When will the TiO2 anti-dumping duty be restored and when will sulphuric acid prices stabilise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a DGTR announcement on TiO2 anti-dumping duty within 1-2 months, but could not predict sulphuric acid price normalisation and hoped the war and Strait of Hormuz disruption end soon.

qa_highlights.question: Can Crop Protection margins reach the long-term range in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated a 15-17% Crop Protection EBITDA margin range for FY27, saying Q4 was hit by inability to pass on price increases that is now gradually easing.

qa_highlights.question: What are the quantified synergies from the amalgamation of Kilburn and Meghmani Crop Nutrition?
qa_highlights.answer: No quantified synergies were given; benefits cited were reduced compliance across entities, combined customer-facing teams, resource optimisation and utilisation of cash held in the subsidiaries. The Court has directed a vote on June 6.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital and capex plan for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: No significant capex; routine capex of INR 35-40 crore. Working capital to improve through inventory rationalisation and lower receivable days.

qa_highlights.question: When will Nano Urea and other Nano products show revenue impact, and are orders in the pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined quarter-wise guidance, saying some orders will come in Q1 and Q2 and the full year will show significant growth; it confirmed existing orders and expects more.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Nano Urea sell-out rate and market share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give sell-out data. It said IFFCO has the upper hand due to conventional urea presence, and Meghmani's Nano product basket is being expanded.

capex_capacity: Crop Protection capacity utilisation about 72% in FY26 on production of about 40,371 MT; Pigments utilisation 40% on about 13,191 MT.
No significant capex planned in FY27; routine capex of INR 35-40 crore.
Nano fertiliser products (Nano DAP, Nano NPK, Nano Zinc) to be made at the existing Sanand, Gujarat facility with no additional capex; Nano Urea made in the same plant.
Management stated Nano Urea capacity is 5 crore bottles per year, correcting an analyst's figure of 2 crore.
TiO2 operations suspended; minimal operating cost retained and no capex planned for the unit.
demand_pricing: Crop Protection is about 78% of FY26 standalone revenue; management expects double-digit top-line growth in FY27 with profitability better than Q4.
Q4 Crop Protection margin about 9% as the company could not pass on raw material price increases immediately after the March geopolitical shock; management said pricing is gradually improving.
Pigments FY27 top line guided at about INR 500-600 crore, with margin expected to be better than FY26's 3.3% as the segment benefits from price increases by competitors and unorganised players.
Demand in the US and Latin America described as good with low channel inventory, but customers are buying in smaller lots due to war-driven price rises.
Rupee depreciation is helping export competitiveness versus China, per management.
Sulphuric acid price is above INR 30/kg versus below INR 10 earlier, and below INR 5 in normal times, making TiO2 unviable.
risks_watch: Crop Protection Q4 margin of about 9% versus FY27 guidance of 15-17%; watch whether price pass-through restores margins in Q1 FY27.
TiO2 suspension: DGTR anti-dumping decision expected in 1-2 months; watch for restart decision and any write-down of the unit.
Sulphur and sulphuric acid cost trajectory linked to the Middle East conflict, affecting TiO2 and other chemical costs.
Nano fertiliser revenue timing is unquantified; management gave no quarter-wise guidance and no sell-out data.
Customers buying in smaller lots due to price caution; watch volumes and inventory levels in the US, Latin America and Europe.
Amalgamation of Kilburn Chemicals and Meghmani Crop Nutrition: court-directed shareholder vote on June 6, with no quantified synergies given.
key_quotes: So on the long-term perspective, we stick to a guideline of 15% to 17%.
There won't be any significant capex in the current financial year.
Currently, the sulphuric acid price is more than INR30 per kg, which used to be below INR10.
So overall, as a year, there will be a good amount of growth.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth, Brazil entry and the FY27 Crop Protection and Pigments recovery, but cautious and often non-specific on quarter-wise timing for Nano products, TiO2 restart and sulphuric acid prices. Management repeatedly declined to give quarter-level numbers, and gave no quantified synergy figures for the amalgamation.

adds.what: Nano fertiliser products (Nano DAP, Nano NPK, Nano Zinc, Nano Urea) at existing Sanand, Gujarat facility, no additional capex

growth.why: Management guides double-digit Crop Protection top-line growth and Pigments FY27 revenue of INR 500-600 crore (vs FY26 INR 461 crore), backed by pricing gains from competitor price rises and a Nano fertiliser launch at existing Sanand plant, but no new capacity or firm orders quantified and Q4 margins remained thin.
